decisions.issues: Minor only. The thumb presses flat on a folded sheaf held in the fist on his white-mundu lap, not on paper laid flat, but the script beat reads clearly: the ridged nail catches the light and the setting matches the courtyard (dappled shade on the stone platform, white mundu, consistent with 3.1 and 4.1). The knuckle is only slightly pale. The ink marks on the paper are soft, blurred smears with no legible glyphs, which fits the 'smeared, seen through tears' treatment in 3.1. The forearm shown is the outer side, so the inner-left scar is correctly out of view. Both captions can go in the top band of dappled stone platform and the upper right above the paper, clear of the thumb and nail. v01 (full face, a second man, kalari background, wide framing) and v02 (legible pseudo-script on the paper) are not listed as candidates and were not considered.

Minor only: the grey at the temple is a fairly broad streak, and there is light tonal shading along the jaw, but the chin reads clean-shaven with no beard. The brand on the inner left forearm cannot be seen because the raised left arm shows its outer side, which is fine at this framing. Everything else matches: thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, high Kerala topknot with no turban, plain white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain, and the ivory conch-handled knife at the waist. He is standing on the laterite-plinth verandah under tiled eaves, with his fingers at the wick of a brass lamp in the wall niche beside the door. The flame lights his face warmly and there is a low moon over palms and glinting channels. The art has no text. The open night sky at upper left gives plenty of space for both captions.
